weeks.title: Two Kinds of Plans
weeks.academic_focus: Algebra readiness, functions, data tables, and explicit assumptions
weeks.arc_turn: Malik and Nia meet, clash over method, and discover that their strengths fit together.
daily_beats: Malik arrives early for Summer Bridge and finds a mistake in the budget he promised his family was finished.
Nia asks to share his table, jokes about the spreadsheet, and recognizes the fear beneath his precision.
A diagnostic modeling task pairs them; Malik wants clean columns while Nia draws the situation before calculating.
Dr. Brooks asks each student why mathematics matters, and Malik and Nia give answers rooted in family and service.
Their campus tour establishes Eliza Moss Hall, Jubilee Library, North Star Learning Commons, and Founders' Bell.
At Indigo Night, Nia meets band saxophonist Julian Cross while Malik signs up for the Heron Analytics information session.
Malik and Nia present a repaired budget model together and agree to be accountability partners for the year.
weeks.handoff: Nia accepts Julian's invitation to the campus radio showcase, and Malik notices that the news disappoints him.

weeks.title: The Shape of an Invitation
weeks.academic_focus: Function notation, domain, range, graph interpretation, and model limitations
weeks.arc_turn: Nia and Julian begin a flirtation while Malik chooses a difficult extracurricular goal of his own.
daily_beats: Nia catches Julian's radio segment about first-year fears and agrees to help him fact-check a math joke.
Malik attends the Heron Analytics orientation and learns that first-years must test into the competitive team.
A domain-and-range exercise exposes how quickly Malik discards messy real-world cases that Nia insists matter.
Julian invites Nia to hear the Marching Herons rehearse, and she says yes before checking her crowded schedule.
Malik tells DJ Cole, his future roommate, that he is interested in the analytics challenge, not in Nia.
At band rehearsal, Nia sees Julian's discipline beneath his public confidence and shares why she chose math.
Nia tells Malik the evening felt like a date; he responds kindly, then stays late preparing for the analytics test.
weeks.handoff: Move-in week will put the new friendship, the new attraction, and Malik's competitive ambition in the same small orbit.

weeks.title: Rooms, Rules, and First Impressions
weeks.academic_focus: Bridge capstone modeling, unit analysis, and communicating a result to a nontechnical audience
weeks.arc_turn: The core supporting cast forms, and Malik learns that competence does not automatically make him a good teammate.
daily_beats: Malik moves in with DJ, whose football schedule and easy sociability immediately disrupt Malik's ideal room plan.
Nia meets roommate Keisha Morgan, a computer science student and sprinter who refuses to let Nia join six clubs in one afternoon.
The Bridge capstone asks Malik and Nia to model shuttle demand during move-in; their first draft ignores accessibility needs.
They interview students instead of defending the model, and the revised assumptions change both the mathematics and the route plan.
Julian films their capstone for campus media and invites Nia to the Heritage Kickoff after the first week of classes.
Malik takes the Heron Analytics screening test and leaves certain that one probability question ruined his chances.
At Opening Convocation, the Founders' Bell rings as the four friends cross Cypress Walk toward the official start of the year.
weeks.handoff: Classes begin, Julian's invitation becomes a real date, and Malik waits for an analytics decision he cannot control.

weeks.title: The First Limit
weeks.academic_focus: Calculus I review, functions, graphical limits, and one-sided behavior
weeks.arc_turn: Nia and Julian step toward a relationship; Malik is selected as an analytics alternate rather than a full member.
daily_beats: Dr. Brooks opens Calculus I with a graph whose value and limiting behavior disagree, unsettling Malik's answer-first habits.
Nia volunteers an explanation, then realizes afterward that she spoke over a quieter classmate.
Malik receives alternate status for Heron Analytics and tells everyone that alternate was what he expected.
DJ asks Malik to help compare two play-call datasets, giving Malik a concrete way to prove he belongs on the team.
Julian and Nia share lunch at Copper Cup Cafe and agree that the Heritage Kickoff will be their first official date.
A group limit problem forces Malik to ask the classmate Nia interrupted to complete the argument.
Malik watches Nia leave with Julian, then turns his disappointment into an overambitious analytics work plan.
weeks.handoff: The opening football weekend will make Nia's romance and Malik's attempt to earn a team seat public.

weeks.title: Kickoff
weeks.academic_focus: Limit laws, infinite limits, continuity, and the first homework-set deadline
weeks.arc_turn: Nia and Julian's first date succeeds, and Malik's useful halftime observation earns him a trial seat on the analytics team.
daily_beats: Malik and Nia finish the first limit set before the Heritage Kickoff, but neither admits they wanted the afternoon together.
At the game, Julian explains band cues to Nia while DJ waits on special teams for a chance that never comes.
Malik spots a fourth-down tendency in the opponent data and sends it to Simone Hart, the analytics team lead.
Nia and Julian walk Cypress Walk after the win and share a gentle first kiss near the closed radio booth.
On Labor Day, Malik learns his observation helped a second-half adjustment and is invited to a two-week team trial.
A continuity problem exposes a hole in Nia's algebra review because she spent the holiday answering club messages.
Nia tells Malik that she and Julian are seeing each other; Malik congratulates her without pretending the news is easy.
weeks.handoff: Malik must prove he belongs on the analytics team while the first Calculus I test approaches.

weeks.title: Continuity Under Pressure
weeks.academic_focus: Continuity, the Intermediate Value Theorem, and the derivative as a limit
weeks.arc_turn: Malik's need to impress causes his first team error, while Nia learns that a new relationship still needs boundaries.
daily_beats: Malik submits an analytics chart without checking a missing-data gap, and Simone makes him explain the error to the team.
Dr. Brooks derives instantaneous rate of change from a limit instead of giving the class a shortcut formula.
Nia cancels a study block when Julian gets unexpected rehearsal time, then resents a choice he did not ask her to make.
Keisha points out that Nia is treating availability as affection and challenges her to restore the study block.
During the road game, DJ makes his college debut on special teams and forces a fumble despite McCall-Hart's loss.
Malik rebuilds the chart with uncertainty labels and earns Simone's respect by showing exactly where the model is weak.
Nia tells Julian she cannot be on call around every rehearsal; he accepts the boundary more easily than she expected.
weeks.handoff: The first major test will show whether their improved decisions arrived soon enough.

weeks.title: What the First Test Measures
weeks.academic_focus: Derivative rules, test one on limits and continuity, and error analysis
weeks.arc_turn: Malik earns a full analytics seat but receives a poor calculus grade; public progress and private shame arrive together.
daily_beats: The home opener fills Henry Boyd Stadium, and DJ's forced fumble earns him a place in the weekly highlight reel.
Malik rushes through the calculus test so he can reach an analytics meeting and fails to justify two limit arguments.
Nia does well but recognizes that her strongest answer came from the classmate she interrupted during week one.
Simone offers Malik a full roster seat based on his corrected model and willingness to own the mistake.
Malik celebrates with DJ, then opens a test score far below anything he has shown his family before.
He tells Nia the exam was fine and avoids Dr. Brooks's office hours, breaking their promise to be honest partners.
Nia finds his abandoned test correction sheet and asks why he trusts her with goals but not with bad news.
weeks.handoff: Before Malik can answer, a Gulf storm begins threatening his family in Gulfport.

weeks.title: No Model for the Storm
weeks.academic_focus: Product, quotient, and chain rules; interpreting changing rates
weeks.arc_turn: The storm turns Malik's academic shame into a family crisis he can no longer manage alone.
daily_beats: Malik's mother reports rising water near their Gulfport home, and he starts refreshing forecasts during calculus.
Dr. Bennett's uncertainty colloquium gives Malik language for ranges and risk but no emotional comfort.
Nia organizes a supply table, then stops herself from taking over when Malik says he needs quiet rather than tasks.
Julian uses campus radio to share verified storm resources, giving Nia a view of him as a responsible partner.
The storm floods the Baptistes' ground floor; Malik's father injures his leg while moving equipment during cleanup.
Malik misses a quiz while trying to arrange transportation home and finally tells Dr. Brooks what happened.
Nia and DJ drive Malik to the bus station, where he admits he does not know what his family will come back to.
weeks.handoff: Malik goes home, leaving coursework, the analytics model, and his feelings for Nia unresolved.

weeks.title: What Water Takes
weeks.academic_focus: Implicit differentiation, related rates, and documented make-up work
weeks.arc_turn: Malik sees the material and financial scale of his family's loss; Nia and Julian become an official couple.
daily_beats: In Gulfport, Malik inventories ruined furniture and school records while his father begins a painful recovery.
A related-rates assignment feels cruelly relevant until Malik uses it to explain rising-water timing to his younger cousin.
Simone divides Malik's analytics work among the team without blaming him, but the loss of control unsettles him.
Back at McCall-Hart, Julian asks Nia to make their relationship official during the Founders' Bell ceremony.
The Founders' Cup game becomes DJ's first extended offensive appearance, and he catches three difficult passes in a win.
Malik returns for an emergency financial-aid appointment and applies for evening work at North Star Learning Commons.
He sees Nia and Julian holding hands, feels both glad and hurt, and chooses not to make Nia manage his disappointment.
weeks.handoff: Malik must balance paid work, make-up calculus, family calls, and an analytics deadline in the same week.

weeks.title: The Cost of Looking Fine
weeks.academic_focus: Linear approximation, differentials, and an applications exam
weeks.arc_turn: Malik's concealment costs him academically, and Nia's habit of overgiving creates friction with Julian.
daily_beats: Malik begins a late shift checking students into North Star and falls asleep over a linearization problem afterward.
He gives the analytics team a polished forecast that hides a wide error range, and Simone refuses to present it.
Nia promises Julian she will attend a media showcase, then agrees to lead an overlapping calculus review without telling him.
The applications exam includes a justification Malik practiced but cannot retrieve after another midnight family call.
Julian learns about Nia's conflict from a flyer and asks why she keeps making him discover her choices in public.
Malik finally shows Nia his poor first test and unfinished make-up work; she listens without turning the moment into a rescue plan.
He tells Dr. Brooks the full truth and accepts a reduced analytics role until his coursework stabilizes.
weeks.handoff: Cypress Week will test whether boundaries and reduced responsibilities survive the loudest week of fall.

weeks.title: Cypress Week
weeks.academic_focus: Critical points, curve sketching, optimization, and interpreting derivative signs
weeks.arc_turn: DJ achieves a public sports breakthrough while Nia and Julian's relationship begins to crack under public obligations.
daily_beats: Nia chooses one homecoming service project instead of five and thinks she has solved her overcommitment problem.
An optimization task asks the class to maximize revenue with constraints, giving Malik a route back into focused work.
Julian's media and band schedules consume every planned date, while he assumes Nia understands because she is also busy.
At Battle of the Bands, Nia watches Julian perform brilliantly but cannot get five private minutes with him afterward.
DJ enters the homecoming game after an injury ahead of him and catches the touchdown that changes his place on the depth chart.
Malik's corrected fourth-down model supports a successful late-game decision, but he credits Simone and the full team publicly.
Nia and Julian argue on Cypress Walk when he posts a perfect homecoming photo that hides how disconnected they felt.
weeks.handoff: The campus returns to ordinary life, where Nia and Julian must decide whether the argument was a bad night or a warning.

weeks.title: The Maximum Is Not the Meaning
weeks.academic_focus: Optimization applications, Mean Value Theorem, and test two corrections
weeks.arc_turn: Malik's team submits a competitive regional model; Nia and Julian repair the surface of their conflict but not its cause.
daily_beats: Dr. Price gives a colloquium on optimizing evacuation routes without treating people as interchangeable points.
Nia recognizes the same error in her own life: maximizing commitments has minimized her attention.
Malik and Simone revise the analytics model around uncertainty intervals instead of a single confident answer.
Julian plans a quiet dinner and apologizes for turning their relationship into content during homecoming.
Nia apologizes for assuming love means endless flexibility, and they agree to protect one private evening each week.
The analytics team submits to the regional semifinal with a model Malik knows is honest rather than unbeatable.
A lab invitation arrives for students to tour Delta National Laboratory, and both Malik and Nia apply for limited seats.
weeks.handoff: The lab trip offers a bigger future just as Malik's home repairs stall and Nia's relationship feels temporarily safe.

weeks.title: Beyond the Campus Map
weeks.academic_focus: Antiderivatives, initial-value problems, and accumulated change
weeks.arc_turn: The first national-lab visit expands both students' ambitions while widening the gap between Nia and Julian.
daily_beats: Malik learns the family insurance claim needs more documentation and uses his work-study break to organize damaged-item evidence.
Dr. Brooks introduces antiderivatives as recovering a possible history from observed rates, with uncertainty in the constant.
Malik and Nia board the Delta National Laboratory bus before dawn and leave Julian's messages unanswered during security orientation.
A scientist demonstrates storm-surge simulation on a supercomputer, connecting Nia's visual instincts with Malik's risk questions.
They attend a presentation by a Black applied mathematician who describes failure as part of model validation, not a character verdict.
On the ride home, Malik and Nia share an intense conversation about work that matters; Julian sees their closeness in Nia's photos.
Julian admits he felt excluded, and Nia hears jealousy where he is also asking to understand a part of her life.
weeks.handoff: Halloween weekend and a major rivalry game will bring Julian, Malik, and Nia into the same crowded spaces.

weeks.title: Riemann Sums and Missing Pieces
weeks.academic_focus: Riemann sums, definite integrals, and estimating totals from incomplete data
weeks.arc_turn: Nia's relationship tension becomes visible to friends, and Malik's analytics team advances to the semifinal.
daily_beats: At a middle-school outreach night, Nia uses rectangles to estimate the area of an irregular paper mask and remembers why she loves teaching.
Julian arrives late to film the event and jokes about Malik and Nia being a matched set, then regrets the edge in his voice.
Malik refuses to engage the joke and tells Julian privately that Nia should not have to defend a friendship to prove a relationship.
During the rivalry game, DJ drops an early pass but catches the fourth-quarter conversion that keeps the winning drive alive.
The analytics team receives semifinal status, and Malik's first instinct is to calculate how little time remains before the presentation.
Nia leaves the basketball exhibition early after Julian turns a disagreement into a performance for his friends.
She tells Keisha that being loved in public is not helping her feel known in private.
weeks.handoff: The semester's withdrawal deadline and semifinal preparation force every character to decide what can still be repaired.

weeks.title: What Can Still Be Changed
weeks.academic_focus: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, net change, and substitution
weeks.arc_turn: Malik learns that his father's recovery will take longer; Nia and Julian stop pretending one date fixed them.
daily_beats: Advising week makes campus conversations unusually honest about grades, money, health, and whether to remain in difficult courses.
Malik's father says he cannot return to work yet, and Malik quietly increases his North Star hours despite Dr. Bennett's warning.
The Fundamental Theorem links accumulation and rate, but Malik cannot reconcile how quickly small losses have accumulated at home.
Simone cuts three slides from Malik's semifinal presentation because his need to prove rigor has buried the decision the model supports.
Nia and Julian attempt their protected private evening and spend most of it arguing about who has been keeping score.
They agree to take several days apart rather than perform another reconciliation before friends.
Malik notices Nia is hurting but keeps the analytics rehearsal, sending one simple message that asks what support she wants.
weeks.handoff: The breakup and Malik's semifinal result will arrive within days of each other.

weeks.title: Two Honest Losses
weeks.academic_focus: Substitution, area between curves, and test three
weeks.arc_turn: Nia's first relationship ends, and Malik's team fails to advance despite a strong presentation.
daily_beats: Nia and Julian meet at the quiet radio booth and admit that affection has not made their needs compatible.
They end the relationship without betrayal or cruelty, leaving Nia with no villain to make the heartbreak easier.
Nia completes the area-between-curves test while fighting the impulse to text Julian after every difficult moment.
At the regional semifinal, Malik presents the uncertainty honestly but cannot answer a judge's question about model transferability.
Another university advances; McCall-Hart does not, and Malik initially blames the answer he gave rather than the model's real limits.
Simone refuses to call the result unfair and asks the team to document what failed before discussing next year.
Malik and Nia sit on opposite ends of a North Star couch, each grieving a different future without trying to fix the other.
weeks.handoff: River Classic and Thanksgiving place public celebration beside private disappointment.

weeks.title: The Catch and the Quiet After
weeks.academic_focus: Applications of definite integrals, cumulative review, and communicating solutions
weeks.arc_turn: DJ's decisive sports success lifts the campus while Nia and Malik begin processing loss instead of hiding it.
daily_beats: Nia returns Julian's spare radio-booth key before his final fall performance and cries only after he leaves.
Malik converts the analytics failure into a clean postmortem instead of a secret file he never opens again.
The River Classic stays tied until DJ catches a difficult sideline pass that sets up the winning score.
Campus celebration carries DJ through interviews, but he calls his mother first because the scholarship implications matter more than attention.
Nia congratulates Julian after the band performance, proving closure can be respectful and still hurt.
Malik goes to Gulfport for Thanksgiving and sees stripped walls, repair estimates, and his father's slow walk through the damaged room.
Nia and Malik speak by phone from separate family kitchens, and neither turns the call into a confession.
weeks.handoff: Finals require both students to carry unresolved emotion into the last Calculus I work of the semester.

weeks.title: The Work Before the Answer
weeks.academic_focus: Comprehensive Calculus I review, proof of reasoning, and final project completion
weeks.arc_turn: Malik accepts that the analytics loss will not be reversed; Nia learns to ask for help while grieving.
daily_beats: Nia returns to a campus full of couple traditions and asks Keisha to stay with her through the first quiet evening.
Malik tells Dr. Bennett he wants to appeal the semifinal score; the professor makes him identify an actual procedural error first.
Finding none, Malik withdraws the appeal and writes the failure into his portfolio with an honest technical analysis.
Nia leads one final review circle but assigns parts to others when her concentration slips instead of performing endless strength.
The football regular season closes with DJ named conference freshman of the week, while he still has a statistics paper due.
At the basketball home opener, Malik and Nia choose a group outing rather than using each other to escape the week's emotions.
They finish a Calculus I review map that shows what each once misunderstood and what still needs work.
weeks.handoff: Finals week will settle grades and a conference football title, but not the emotional story.

weeks.title: Everything That Counts
weeks.academic_focus: Calculus I final examination and explanation-based review
weeks.arc_turn: The fall ends with an athletic championship and credible academic recovery, but no romantic shortcut.
daily_beats: On the last class day, Dr. Brooks returns Malik's corrected first test beside his recent work so the improvement is visible without being perfect.
McCall-Hart wins the conference football championship, and DJ contributes a difficult third-down catch rather than a storybook final touchdown.
Nia celebrates with friends, then leaves before Julian's band gathering because she knows the night would reopen the breakup.
The Calculus I final asks students to connect a graph, derivative, and accumulated area in one argument.
Malik slows down enough to finish every justification, accepting that one unanswered part does not invalidate the work he completed.
Nia freezes on an integration setup, uses the remaining time to redraw the region, and recovers without looking to anyone else.
After the final, Malik and Nia exchange no promises beyond getting home safely and telling each other the truth about results.
weeks.handoff: Winter break begins with a bowl trip for DJ, a damaged home for Malik, and a first holiday after heartbreak for Nia.

weeks.title: After the Grades
weeks.academic_focus: Fall reflection, transcript review, and identifying concrete spring prerequisites
weeks.arc_turn: DJ receives a scholarship increase, and Malik earns a solid recovery without the competition victory he wanted.
daily_beats: Fall commencement lets the first-years see families celebrate work whose difficulty is invisible in a ceremony program.
The Herons win the Heritage Bowl, and DJ's blocking assignment on the decisive play matters more than the ball going elsewhere.
DJ learns his scholarship will increase in spring and calls Malik before the announcement becomes public.
Malik opens a B in Calculus I and initially sees only the distance from the grade he expected in August.
Nia earns an A-minus but does not use it to erase how exhausted and heartbroken she became.
At an alumni actuarial workshop, Simone and Malik debrief the analytics loss and discover how easy their conversation feels without a deadline.
Malik returns to Gulfport and sleeps in the living room because his old room still smells like removed drywall.
weeks.handoff: Separate holidays give Malik and Nia room to become more than each other's primary support.

weeks.title: Christmas Without the Old Version
weeks.academic_focus: Rest, family responsibility, and a light preview of integration applications
weeks.arc_turn: Nia grieves the relationship without returning to it, while Malik stops treating care for her as a claim on her future.
daily_beats: Nia finds Julian's handmade playlist in a box and allows herself to miss the good parts without calling the breakup a mistake.
Her mother asks whether she misses Julian or misses being chosen, and Nia admits she cannot separate the answers yet.
Malik helps his father complete physical-therapy exercises and sees how humiliating dependence feels to someone proud of providing.
A contractor delay pushes repairs into spring, forcing the family to decide which damaged rooms can wait.
Malik texts Nia a photo of a badly shaped homemade pie instead of checking whether she is lonely.
Nia spends Christmas with family and leaves her phone in another room through dinner for the first time all fall.
Both write spring goals that include people, sleep, and uncertainty rather than only outcomes.
weeks.handoff: The new year begins with Malik ready to move forward and Nia not yet realizing she will mind when he does.

weeks.title: The Year Turns Quietly
weeks.academic_focus: Calculus II readiness: antiderivative fluency, graph interpretation, and algebra repair
weeks.arc_turn: Malik chooses to stop waiting for Nia, and Nia applies for a research opportunity that will define spring.
daily_beats: Malik completes the analytics postmortem and sends Simone a thank-you that becomes an hour-long phone conversation.
Nia reads a call for flood-resilience research proposals inspired by the fall Delta National Laboratory visit.
Keisha agrees to code for the project only if Nia treats her as a collaborator rather than emergency technical help.
Malik removes a private calendar reminder labeled tell Nia after finals and accepts that no perfect moment is owed to him.
Nia and Julian exchange brief New Year's messages that are warm, final, and free of hidden invitations.
At midnight, Nia calls Malik and hears Simone laughing in the background of a group video chat.
Nia tells herself the sharp feeling is surprise, then opens the research application instead of calling back.
weeks.handoff: Spring returns with a reversed emotional current and two new partnerships.

weeks.title: The First Return
weeks.academic_focus: Calculus II orientation, accumulated area review, and applications of integration
weeks.arc_turn: Malik and Simone reconnect in person, and Nia joins Dr. Price's flood-model research group.
daily_beats: Malik returns to a reorganized room where DJ's bowl trophy sits beside an unfinished economics assignment.
Nia and Keisha pitch the evacuation-model idea at research matching and are assigned a skeptical graduate mentor.
Simone asks Malik to coffee before classes begin, making clear that the invitation is personal rather than an analytics debrief.
Malik tells Nia about the coffee without asking permission, and her too-bright approval confuses both of them.
Dr. Delgado opens Calculus II by asking what an integral can measure besides area and rejects five memorized answers.
Nia's first research dataset contains missing road-capacity values that make the proposed model impossible to run as written.
Malik and Simone's coffee extends into dinner, while Nia stays late deciding which research question can survive the data.
weeks.handoff: The first full spring week turns Malik's date and Nia's research idea into commitments.

weeks.title: Volumes and Openings
weeks.academic_focus: Area, volume by disks and washers, and shell-method reasoning
event_anchors: Malik and Simone's first official date
weeks.arc_turn: Malik begins the spring relationship; Nia recognizes that her reaction is more than protective friendship.
daily_beats: Dr. Delgado makes the class choose between washer and shell methods before allowing any computation.
Nia's project team maps flood zones as rotated regions and discovers the most elegant picture does not match the available roads.
At the women's basketball game, Imani introduces Nia to the pressure of making a choice after a visible error.
The men's game runs late, and Malik still leaves on time for his date with Simone instead of making her wait behind campus energy.
Simone asks what Malik wants outside achievement; he gives an honest, unfinished answer about stability and family.
Nia sees Malik return smiling and realizes she had expected him to remain emotionally where she left him in fall.
She tells Keisha she may have feelings for Malik, and Keisha refuses to turn that discovery into a plan to interfere.
weeks.handoff: MLK service weekend will make Malik and Simone visible as a couple while Nia begins her own competitive application.

weeks.title: Work Worth Doing
weeks.academic_focus: Arc length, surface area, and work integrals
event_anchors: Martin Luther King Jr. service day
weeks.arc_turn: Malik and Simone become official, and Nia commits her flood model to the regional symposium track.
daily_beats: The friends volunteer at a neighborhood food distribution site where Nia notices route congestion the research map omitted.
Simone and Malik work the same station well together and agree afterward that they are dating exclusively.
Nia congratulates them sincerely, then takes a long route back to campus so she does not have to perform being unaffected.
A work-integral problem gives Nia a concrete way to include distance, load, and access in the evacuation project.
Dr. Price tells the team the regional symposium will judge a question and method, not the nobility of their intentions.
Keisha agrees to enter as coauthor after Nia rewrites the application to name her coding and data decisions explicitly.
Malik finds Nia's draft in the shared lab, praises its sharper question, and leaves before she can turn the exchange intimate.
weeks.handoff: The research challenge now has a deadline, while Malik's relationship has boundaries Nia must respect.

weeks.title: Choosing a Method
weeks.academic_focus: Integration by parts and method selection
weeks.arc_turn: Nia's project survives its first serious audit, and Malik begins investing in a relationship rather than merely enjoying one.
daily_beats: Dr. Delgado presents three integrals that look alike but require different decisions, frustrating students who want a recipe.
Keisha finds duplicate evacuation records that make Nia's encouraging first graph unreliable.
Nia discards the graph in front of the team instead of hiding the flaw until after the application deadline.
Malik attends Simone's data-finance panel and asks a question that supports her work without redirecting attention to himself.
At the basketball game, Nia sits with Julian by coincidence and discovers they can discuss band travel without relitigating the breakup.
Malik sees them together, notices his old jealousy, and chooses to ask Nia about it directly rather than assume.
Nia says the conversation was closure, then recognizes that she wants Malik to care for reasons she has no right to demand.
weeks.handoff: A difficult integration unit and the first research selection will test all three new boundaries.

weeks.title: Identity in the Integral
weeks.academic_focus: Trigonometric integrals, trigonometric substitution, and algebraic identities
weeks.arc_turn: Nia's proposal advances to the campus round, and Keisha's independent success prevents the research team from becoming Nia's possession.
daily_beats: Nia misapplies a trig identity on the board and must let another student finish the solution she began confidently.
The research proposal advances, but reviewer notes say the human decision assumptions are still vague.
Keisha leaves rehearsal early for an indoor track meet after Nia assumes the team will work through the weekend.
Keisha runs a personal best, reminding Nia that her collaborator has goals that do not orbit the project.
Malik and Simone take a short road trip to a basketball game and discover they disagree about planning every hour of travel.
They laugh through the disagreement rather than treating compatibility as sameness.
Nia rewrites the research schedule around shared ownership and asks Julian to advise only on public visualization.
weeks.handoff: A research conference and Calculus II test arrive during the opening of spring sports.

weeks.title: The Room Beyond the Classroom
weeks.academic_focus: Partial fractions, numerical integration, and test one
weeks.arc_turn: Nia encounters real undergraduate research culture and decides she wants the fellowship, not merely the experience.
daily_beats: The Calculus II test asks students to choose and justify an integration method before computing.
Nia leaves one partial-fractions problem incomplete but writes a correct setup instead of filling the page with guesses.
At the Mathematics Futures Conference, first-year students present imperfect projects and answer serious questions.
A panel on national laboratories shows Nia that mathematical communication can influence infrastructure decisions.
Imani opens softball season with an error and a game-winning double, refusing the reporter's attempt to erase one with the other.
Nia tells Keisha she wants the symposium fellowship badly enough that losing will hurt; Keisha says that honesty will improve the work.
Malik misses the conference for a planned day with Simone but reads Nia's notes later without making the choice a moral test.
weeks.handoff: Valentine's week will make the reversed romantic positions impossible for Nia to ignore.

weeks.title: Valentine's Data
weeks.academic_focus: Improper integrals, convergence of unbounded quantities, and test corrections
weeks.arc_turn: Malik and Simone deepen their relationship, while Nia's first public research pitch exposes a major weakness.
daily_beats: Nia jokes through Valentine's displays until a campus-radio dedication reminds her how much she once wanted public romance.
Malik gives Simone a small notebook containing questions they have not yet had time to answer, not a grand public gesture.
Nia pitches the flood model and is asked why the team assumes every driver receives and trusts the same warning.
She becomes defensive, and Keisha answers the question more honestly than Nia does.
At baseball's opening series, a delayed weather alert gives the team a real example of unequal information flow.
Julian offers to test message designs with campus-media volunteers, and Nia accepts under a written project role.
Nia apologizes to Keisha for treating criticism like disloyalty and rebuilds the proposal around communication failure.
weeks.handoff: A national-lab preview and the transition to infinite sequences will expand the project's scale.

weeks.title: The First Infinite Question
weeks.academic_focus: Sequences, monotonicity, boundedness, and limits of sequences
weeks.arc_turn: The summer lab path opens, and Simone's international ambition introduces a future Malik did not include in his plans.
daily_beats: Dr. Delgado introduces sequences by asking whether repeated small updates approach a stable warning time.
Delta National Laboratory scientists brief students on summer storm-surge work and require multidisciplinary teams.
Nia reshapes the project toward iterative route updates instead of one static evacuation map.
Simone tells Malik she applied for a summer internship in London and does not soften how badly she wants it.
Malik supports the application but privately calculates how a long-distance relationship could fit before asking whether she wants one.
Baseball and softball overlaps force Imani, DJ, and Keisha to trade study coverage rather than attend every event together.
Nia sees Malik and Simone planning interview practice and recognizes that loving someone's ambition can move them away from you.
weeks.handoff: Series and convergence tests will parallel, but not replace, decisions about which efforts can continue.

weeks.title: What Converges
weeks.academic_focus: Infinite series, geometric series, divergence, and the integral test
weeks.arc_turn: Nia's team reaches the regional presentation stage, and Malik realizes Simone's summer plans may not include their relationship.
daily_beats: Nia connects a geometric series to repeated warning reach, then learns the model still overestimates households with limited internet access.
Julian records community interviews that contradict the team's assumptions about trust and official messages.
The project wins the campus semifinal because the team names what it does not yet know.
McCall-Hart's women win the rivalry basketball finale, while the men's team loses on a final missed shot.
The shared crowd must hold triumph and disappointment without reducing either team to the other's result.
Simone receives a London interview and tells Malik she cannot promise a summer decision before she has an offer.
Malik asks whether they are planning a relationship or preserving a pleasant semester, and Simone says they need more evidence.
weeks.handoff: Conference tournament pressure and spring break will separate the characters long enough to expose mistaken assumptions.

weeks.title: Tests of Convergence
weeks.academic_focus: Comparison, ratio, root, and alternating-series tests
weeks.arc_turn: Nia earns a symposium place while Malik and Simone begin confronting an incompatibility that affection cannot solve.
daily_beats: Dr. Delgado requires students to defend which convergence test they chose before showing any algebra.
Nia's team receives regional symposium acceptance and a final-round fellowship interview slot.
Julian designs an animated route map that makes the research understandable without turning Nia into the project's sole hero.
McCall-Hart's women's basketball team reaches the conference final, and Keisha travels with the student pep group after completing her code review.
The women lose a close final but earn a postseason invitation, giving campus a future beyond the immediate result.
Simone's London interview goes well; Malik congratulates her, then admits he hoped the opportunity would become less real.
They decide not to force a spring breakup before they know the offer, but the relationship no longer feels uncomplicated.
weeks.handoff: Spring break brings Nia and Julian into close project work and gives Malik too much room to misread it.

weeks.title: Spring Break, Old Angles
weeks.academic_focus: Power-series preview, approximation error, and research revision
weeks.arc_turn: Julian and Nia prove they can collaborate without reuniting, while Malik's jealousy reveals feelings he has not resolved.
daily_beats: Nia stays on campus for two break days to rebuild the presentation with Keisha and Julian.
Julian interviews Nia about the breakup between elegant models and messy human behavior, and the answer applies to more than research.
A still image of Nia and Julian laughing over edits reaches Malik without the context of the full team in the room.
Malik says nothing and becomes distant during Simone's interview practice, making her pay for a feeling she did not cause.
Simone asks directly whether Malik is jealous of Julian; Malik admits he is and does not defend it.
Nia goes home to Huntsville and tells her mother that working with Julian felt safe precisely because the relationship is over.
The friends return to campus with a stronger project, a strained spring relationship, and no romantic confrontation yet.
weeks.handoff: A Delta National Laboratory visit will force the research team and both romantic histories into one trip.

weeks.title: Radius of Influence
weeks.academic_focus: Power series, radius and interval of convergence, and approximation error
weeks.arc_turn: The lab visit validates the project direction, while Simone sees that Malik and Nia's connection is unresolved.
daily_beats: Nia uses a power-series approximation to speed one local calculation and must state where the approximation stops being reliable.
At Delta National Laboratory, the team tours the supercomputing floor and hears a talk on uncertainty communication.
Malik joins the trip as an actuarial student and asks how agencies price rare risks without pretending the estimates are certain.
Nia and Malik co-answer a scientist's question with the old ease that first formed during Summer Bridge.
Simone watches the exchange without blaming Nia and later asks Malik whether part of him has remained unavailable all spring.
Keisha opens outdoor track with a strong relay split, while Imani's softball team sweeps a road series after two one-run games.
Malik tells Simone he does not know what his connection with Nia means, which is honest but not harmless.
weeks.handoff: Nia's final rehearsal and Simone's internship decision will remove the shelter of uncertainty.

weeks.title: Approximation Is Not Arrival
weeks.academic_focus: Taylor and Maclaurin series, polynomial approximation, and error bounds
weeks.arc_turn: Nia's polished presentation fails in rehearsal, and Simone receives the offer that makes her spring choice concrete.
daily_beats: Nia gives a technically dense rehearsal that leaves a community reviewer unable to say what decision the model supports.
Dr. Price stops the talk at minute six and tells Nia that correctness without audience understanding is unfinished work.
Julian removes half the animation rather than adding spectacle, and Keisha rewrites the live demonstration around one household's choices.
Simone receives the London offer and accepts before discussing it with Malik because the career decision is hers.
Malik is proud and hurt, then recognizes that he had treated consultation as proof of commitment.
Imani commits an error in the softball rivalry opener and responds with disciplined defense in the next two games, not a miraculous home run.
Nia's second rehearsal lands, but she learns that a strong performance still cannot guarantee the fellowship.
weeks.handoff: Withdrawal week, parametric motion, and Simone's decision will bring the spring relationship to its end.

weeks.title: Different Parameters
weeks.academic_focus: Parametric equations, velocity, acceleration, and arc length
weeks.arc_turn: Simone ends the relationship with agency and care; Malik refuses to move immediately toward Nia.
daily_beats: Parametric curves show the class how two quantities can share time without following the same path.
Simone tells Malik that London is not the only issue: she has felt him comparing their relationship with an unfinished possibility.
Malik apologizes without asking her to stay and admits he entered spring believing moving forward meant never looking back.
They end the relationship at Porter Center, sad and respectful, with no promise to resume after summer.
Nia hears about the breakup from Malik himself and feels hope followed immediately by guilt.
When Nia hints that they should talk about fall, Malik says he will not turn her heartbreak or his into a shortcut.
The research team submits its final symposium materials as Malik and Nia agree to protect distance through the presentation.
weeks.handoff: Nia must face the fellowship judges without using romance, reconciliation, or Malik as emotional proof that she is okay.

weeks.title: The Presentation and the No
weeks.academic_focus: Polar coordinates, polar area, and choosing coordinate systems for a problem
weeks.arc_turn: Nia gives the strongest talk she can and does not receive the national fellowship.
daily_beats: Nia uses polar coordinates to explain why distance from a warning source is not the same as access to a safe route.
The team travels to the symposium and watches projects with more funding, older students, and cleaner datasets.
Keisha runs the live model, Julian manages the visual sequence, and Nia answers questions without claiming certainty the data cannot support.
The judges praise the public-value question and identify unresolved validation gaps.
Another team receives the national fellowship, and Nia applauds before finding a private stairwell where disappointment can be honest.
Malik waits outside rather than entering until Keisha confirms Nia wants him there.
Nia says she did everything better and still lost; Malik answers that the loss is real and does not need a lesson tonight.
weeks.handoff: The final class week asks Nia what remains valuable when the desired award is gone.

weeks.title: What Remains
weeks.academic_focus: Calculus II synthesis, polar review, and final-project interpretation
weeks.arc_turn: Nia keeps the research alive without pretending she has recovered, and both old relationships receive clear closure.
daily_beats: Nia considers deleting the project folder, then archives the fellowship version and opens a new file labeled community validation.
A public-mathematics speaker explains how rejected academic work can become useful only after researchers relinquish ownership.
Julian asks whether their successful collaboration means they should try dating again; Nia says no without punishing him for asking.
Simone and Malik exchange internship logistics and return personal items without rewriting spring as a mistake.
Imani's softball team wins its home finale and qualifies for the conference tournament, while baseball loses its series.
Malik and Nia admit they wanted each other at different times and agree that timing alone is not enough to build trust.
They choose to focus on finals and let summer reveal who they are when neither is waiting in the wings.
weeks.handoff: Final examinations close the reversed spring arcs but leave the central relationship deliberately unresolved.

weeks.title: No Shortcut Through Finals
weeks.academic_focus: Calculus II final examination: integration methods, series, parametric equations, and polar coordinates
weeks.arc_turn: Malik and Nia finish spring independently and both receive summer opportunities tied to the rejected project.
daily_beats: The Calculus II final begins with method selection, forcing students to commit before computation offers reassurance.
Malik catches himself rushing an integration-by-parts problem and restarts the setup even though the clock is moving.
Nia identifies a divergent series correctly, then spends too long proving it because she no longer trusts good instinct after the fellowship loss.
After the exam, Dr. Delgado refuses grade speculation and asks them what work they would still choose without points attached.
Imani's walk-off single in the softball rivalry series secures a tournament seed and gives the group one uncomplicated celebration.
Dr. Price invites Nia and Keisha to continue the evacuation model in the summer program, contingent on community validation.
Dr. Bennett invites Malik to join the same project as a risk-modeling assistant, and Malik asks for a day before answering.
weeks.handoff: The summer invitation offers proximity, not romantic resolution.

weeks.title: The Space Between Semesters
weeks.academic_focus: Final grade reflection and Calculus III readiness
weeks.arc_turn: Both students accept the summer program but agree to begin as separate researchers, not an assumed pair.
daily_beats: Spring grades confirm that Malik and Nia passed Calculus II strongly, but neither result changes the relationship choices they made.
At commencement, Nia watches student researchers graduate and feels grief for the fellowship without questioning her place in mathematics.
Imani's softball team reaches the tournament semifinal and loses after its most successful season in years.
The team celebrates seniors and names the loss honestly, giving Nia another model for pride without a trophy.
Simone leaves for internship orientation and asks Malik to let their relationship remain meaningful without keeping it half-alive.
Malik accepts the summer risk-modeling role; Nia accepts the project-lead role only after Keisha's co-lead title is confirmed.
They leave campus for a short break with one agreement: no private promises before the work begins.
weeks.handoff: Summer brings them back to Eliza Moss Hall for Calculus III and a project neither can complete alone.

weeks.title: Vectors and Boundaries
weeks.academic_focus: Calculus III vectors, three-dimensional coordinates, magnitude, and direction
weeks.arc_turn: Malik and Nia reunite as project colleagues and set explicit boundaries before old ease can decide for them.
daily_beats: Malik returns from Gulfport with photographs of repaired framing but no date for moving the family back into the damaged rooms.
Nia arrives with the rejected symposium poster rolled under her arm and refuses to hide its fellowship label.
At orientation, Dr. Okafor assigns Nia to model lead, Keisha to computation lead, and Malik to risk and validation.
The first Calculus III class uses vectors to separate magnitude from direction, exposing how often the students confuse intensity with progress.
Malik and Nia write collaboration rules covering late-night work, private conversations, and disagreement in front of the team.
Baseball's final road series ends outside postseason qualification, and the seniors return to campus without a final home celebration.
Malik and Nia solve the first vector assignment efficiently, then leave separately instead of extending the night by habit.
weeks.handoff: The team's first technical disagreement will test whether written boundaries survive real pressure.

weeks.title: Lines That Do Not Meet
weeks.academic_focus: Dot products, cross products, lines, planes, and distances in space
weeks.arc_turn: The team discovers that Malik's risk metric and Nia's access metric optimize different outcomes.
daily_beats: A lines-and-planes exercise shows how two paths can be nonparallel and still never intersect.
Malik proposes minimizing expected travel time, while Nia argues that the model must protect neighborhoods with the fewest route choices.
Their first design review becomes personal when Malik says Nia is preserving the rejected proposal instead of testing it.
Nia counters that Malik is optimizing away the people whose data are hardest to price.
Keisha stops the argument and requires each of them to write the other's objective function accurately before responding.
At the baseball home finale, the group honors a losing season's seniors and sees how value can outlast the standings.
Malik and Nia return with a two-metric model that makes the tradeoff visible rather than pretending it disappeared.
weeks.handoff: Community interviews will show whether either metric describes how residents actually move.

weeks.title: Motion in the Real World
weeks.academic_focus: Vector-valued functions, velocity, acceleration, curvature, and motion in space
weeks.arc_turn: The project shifts from abstract routes to household decisions, and Malik begins speaking openly about his family's storm loss.
daily_beats: Residents describe changing routes as water, traffic, and information shift, invalidating the team's fixed-path assumption.
Nia recognizes vector-valued motion in the interviews and redesigns the model around updates over time.
Malik tells the advisory group that his family's flooded home is why he distrusts clean averages, surprising Nia with the public honesty.
On Memorial Day, the students pause data collection and join a community remembrance event rather than treating the holiday as spare work time.
Keisha builds a motion simulation that exposes unrealistic acceleration whenever the model reroutes too many cars at once.
Julian records audio only after every participant chooses how their words may be used, applying the lesson from his spring role.
Nia thanks Malik for naming the personal stake; he says trust now means telling the team, not only telling her.
weeks.handoff: Delta National Laboratory will test the revised model against a much larger simulation.

weeks.title: The Gradient Trip
weeks.academic_focus: Functions of several variables, partial derivatives, gradients, and directional derivatives
weeks.arc_turn: The national-lab visit gives the extracurricular arc real substance and brings Malik and Nia into their first fully honest private conversation.
daily_beats: Dr. Okafor introduces partial derivatives by changing one risk factor while holding the others fixed, then asks when that assumption is impossible.
The team travels to Delta National Laboratory and completes security, ethics, and data-governance orientation before seeing the computers.
A scientist maps the gradient of storm-surge height and shows why fastest increase is not always the safest escape direction.
Keisha ports a small version of the model to the lab system, where its run time fails under the larger road network.
Malik presents the risk assumptions to scientists who challenge the insurance data's bias toward documented property loss.
Nia presents the access metric and admits the model cannot yet represent people without private vehicles.
On the hotel terrace, Malik and Nia discuss Julian, Simone, jealousy, and missed timing without asking for a romantic decision.
weeks.handoff: They return closer, but the model and Malik's family repairs both demand decisions before intimacy.

weeks.title: Tangent to Home
weeks.academic_focus: Tangent planes, linear approximation, multivariable chain rules, and local error
weeks.arc_turn: Nia enters Malik's family world during the final repair push, and local approximation becomes a practical project compromise.
daily_beats: The lab benchmark shows the full model is too slow for emergency use, forcing the team to consider a faster local approximation.
Malik resists approximation because the fall analytics loss taught him to fear a judge finding any simplification.
Dr. Okafor asks whether a slower exact answer delivered after evacuation begins is more responsible than a bounded approximation delivered in time.
Malik's mother announces that the family can move back into the repaired rooms if enough furniture is returned over the weekend.
Nia, Keisha, DJ, and Imani travel to Gulfport to help, meeting Malik's family without framing the visit as charity.
Nia sees the waterline still marked inside a closet and understands why Malik treats uncertainty as a threat to people he loves.
The team chooses a local approximation with published error bounds, and Malik chooses to name his fear rather than disguise it as rigor.
weeks.handoff: An optimization exam and a nearly private moment force Malik and Nia to decide whether closeness is outrunning clarity.

weeks.title: The Constraint Is Real
weeks.academic_focus: Multivariable extrema, Lagrange multipliers, and constrained optimization
weeks.arc_turn: Malik and Nia acknowledge mutual attraction but refuse to begin a relationship in the middle of unresolved project pressure.
daily_beats: A Lagrange-multiplier problem makes the class optimize safety under limited buses, road capacity, time, and staffing.
The community advisory group rejects a route that is mathematically efficient but crosses a chronically flooded underpass.
Nia accepts the correction without defending how much work produced the route.
During poster preparation, Malik and Nia reach for the same marker, laugh, and almost kiss in an empty lab.
Malik stops and says he wants their first decision to happen outside the fluorescent light of a deadline.
Nia admits she wants him too but will not treat wanting as sufficient evidence that they are ready.
They complete the Summer A exam and schedule one actual date after Summer B begins, with no project materials allowed.
weeks.handoff: Juneteenth and the summer break let the rejected spring work serve people before it earns any new academic recognition.

weeks.title: Freedom Is a Practice
weeks.academic_focus: Summer A synthesis and translating mathematical work for public use
weeks.arc_turn: Nia's failed fellowship project becomes a useful public workshop without being converted into an award.
daily_beats: On Juneteenth, the team runs a community table where families compare evacuation choices using a floor-size map.
Children move route markers in ways the model never predicted, exposing assumptions while making the mathematics approachable.
Nia credits Keisha, Julian, Malik, and neighborhood advisors by role instead of presenting the project as her personal comeback.
Malik's father attends and tells him that modeling risk cannot prevent every loss but can help families act sooner.
Summer A grades arrive; both students pass strongly, and the result receives one dinner rather than a week of identity claims.
Julian sends Nia the finished community-audio piece and says their collaboration helped him understand why the breakup was right.
Nia and Malik spend the final break day apart on purpose so their scheduled date can begin as a choice, not momentum.
weeks.handoff: Summer B opens with double integrals, a first date, and the first serious field test of the model.

weeks.title: The First Date, Again
weeks.academic_focus: Double integrals, iterated integration, planar regions, and polar conversion
weeks.arc_turn: Malik and Nia finally go on a date, but delay labels until they discuss what a relationship would require.
daily_beats: Summer B begins with a double integral over an irregular floodplain rather than a rectangular textbook region.
The team divides the region into workable pieces, accepting that different descriptions can represent the same area.
Malik and Nia meet at a small Bellwether bookstore for a date with no laptops, project talk, or friends as witnesses.
They discuss what they admired and misunderstood during each other's fall and spring relationships.
Nia states that she will not become Malik's proof that the spring breakup had a purpose; Malik agrees.
A campus emergency-tabletop exercise exposes a bottleneck near Ruth Ellis Fieldhouse that their model missed.
They end the week with a second date planned and an agreement that honesty, not exclusivity, is the immediate commitment.
weeks.handoff: A family holiday and three-dimensional integration will ask whether the relationship can enter ordinary life.

weeks.title: A Place at the Table
weeks.academic_focus: Triple integrals, cylindrical coordinates, spherical coordinates, mass, and density
weeks.arc_turn: Malik and Nia choose an exclusive relationship after their connection survives family, disagreement, and unglamorous work.
daily_beats: Triple integrals force the class to describe a three-dimensional region before calculating anything inside it.
Nia joins the Baptiste family cookout and helps Malik's younger cousin build a density experiment with fruit and a kitchen scale.
Malik's mother thanks Nia for the repair weekend but makes clear that Malik's healing cannot become Nia's assignment.
A field sensor fails during the project test, and Malik and Nia disagree sharply about whether to interpolate or discard the run.
They bring the dispute to Keisha, accept her decision to preserve the failed run, and return to the date without carrying punishment.
Malik asks Nia to be his partner in language that names affection, uncertainty, and choice rather than fate.
Nia says yes, then tells him they still have to learn how to be together when no crisis is making them important to each other.
weeks.handoff: The new relationship faces an emergency drill where the project must perform under time pressure.

weeks.title: A Field With Consequences
weeks.academic_focus: Vector fields, conservative fields, potential functions, and line integrals
weeks.arc_turn: The model contributes to a real preparedness exercise, and Malik avoids turning renewed analytics interest into a promise of redemption.
daily_beats: Dr. Okafor uses wind and water vector fields to distinguish what acts everywhere from what a traveler experiences along one path.
During Bellwether's emergency drill, the team's dashboard recommends opening a secondary shelter before the main route reaches capacity.
A delayed data feed makes the recommendation arrive late, and the team logs the failure instead of editing the demonstration afterward.
City staff still adopt the two-metric display for future exercises because it makes tradeoffs understandable.
Dr. Bennett invites Malik to speak at a preseason athletics analytics workshop about the fall model's failure.
Malik presents overfitting and transferability errors without turning the talk into a comeback announcement.
Nia attends as his partner but asks no questions from the audience, allowing his work to stand outside their relationship.
weeks.handoff: The Summer Scholars preliminary review will decide whether the project is ready for a public showcase.

weeks.title: Around the Boundary
weeks.academic_focus: Green's Theorem, circulation, flux, and boundary orientation
weeks.arc_turn: The project earns a showcase slot only after leadership is distributed visibly across the team.
daily_beats: Green's Theorem gives the class two ways to describe behavior inside a region and around its boundary.
Nia structures the preliminary review so Keisha demonstrates code, Malik explains risk, and residents respond before Nia concludes.
A reviewer asks whether the model can be maintained after the students leave, exposing a sustainability gap.
Keisha proposes an open documentation plan and presents it at the student-developer forum under her own name.
The community advisory group votes to support a limited pilot, with conditions about privacy and public reporting.
The Summer Scholars committee grants a showcase slot but requests a live failure scenario rather than a polished replay.
Malik and Nia celebrate with friends, then keep their planned private dinner instead of letting the project consume the relationship.
weeks.handoff: The final theorem unit and live failure test will determine what they can responsibly claim.

weeks.title: What Crosses the Surface
weeks.academic_focus: Parametric surfaces, surface integrals, Stokes' Theorem, and the Divergence Theorem
weeks.arc_turn: The model fails safely in public, and the students define success as transparent limits plus useful decisions.
daily_beats: Surface integrals let the class quantify flow across a boundary, giving the project a better shelter-capacity measure.
During the live failure test, Keisha cuts one data source and the model initially recommends an impossible road.
The validation layer Malik built flags the recommendation before it reaches the public display.
Nia explains the failure and fallback process to reviewers without calling the safeguard proof that the system cannot fail.
The team passes the Calculus III project review and receives permission to present the pilot at the showcase.
Second-year registration creates the first real scheduling disagreement in Malik and Nia's relationship because their required courses barely overlap.
They choose schedules that serve their majors and reserve shared time afterward, refusing to make proximity the measure of commitment.
weeks.handoff: Final exams and the showcase will close the academic year while opening next year's choices.

weeks.title: The Work Leaves Their Hands
weeks.academic_focus: Calculus III final examination and integrated vector-calculus interpretation
weeks.arc_turn: The project becomes a community-owned pilot, and both students receive next-step invitations without guaranteed success.
daily_beats: The Calculus III final asks students to connect a vector field, boundary theorem, coordinate system, and physical interpretation.
Nia finishes with time to check orientation signs, a detail she once would have sacrificed to explain more ideas.
Malik catches an unjustified assumption and corrects it even though the revised answer is less elegant.
At the Summer Scholars Showcase, residents describe how the dashboard changed their questions instead of endorsing it as a finished solution.
The team hands documentation and a limited pilot license to the Bellwether emergency office and community advisory group.
Nia is invited to present the community-validation method next year; the invitation does not replace the fellowship she lost.
Malik is invited to reapply for the Heron Analytics team as a peer mentor, and he accepts the application rather than assuming the role.
weeks.handoff: A three-day epilogue at Founders' Bell turns accomplishment toward the unfinished second year.

weeks.title: The Bell Before Year Two
weeks.academic_focus: Reflection, handoff, and second-year intentions
weeks.arc_turn: Family, academic, athletic, and romantic arcs reach honest resolution without pretending the future is solved.
daily_beats: Summer grades arrive, and Malik and Nia share the news with their families before sharing it publicly.
At Founders' Bell, DJ, Keisha, Imani, Julian, Simone by video, and the faculty mark what changed without ranking whose year mattered most.
Malik and Nia walk Cypress Walk as a couple, compare second-year schedules, and look forward to a future they will choose rather than predict.
weeks.handoff: Season one ends with the Founders' Bell ringing for the next class of students.
